answer: The glacier multiplier is published, charged in copper, and vine lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 1625 identities would post 3182 proofs and burn roughly 49 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
